summary: Christopher D. Wallis specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Rochester (BA), Oxford (MPhil under Alexis Sanderson), and UC Berkeley (PhD, 2014, under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt), later serving as guest lecturer at Naropa University.

Christopher Framarin is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi (-2001) and a PhD at the University of New Mexico (-2005). He held faculty posts at the University of Calgary (attested 2014, 2026).
Christopher Hatchell is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia, where he studied under academic mentor David Germano.

Christopher I. Beckwith works in Tibetology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. After degrees at Ohio State (BA) and Indiana University (MA, PhD under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu), he joined Indiana University Bloomington, becoming Professor of Central Eurasian Studies in 1982.

Christopher Ives is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He served as Assistant Professor of Religion at the University of Puget Sound (~1987–2000) and later became professor and chair of religious studies at Stonehill College (~2000).

Christopher Jon Jensen specializes in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Saskatchewan, Kyoto University, and McMaster University (PhD, 2018), working under doctoral supervisor James A. Benn alongside teachers Toru Funayama, Shayne Clarke, Mark Rowe, and Noel Salmond.

Christopher Kelley is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his PhD at Columbia University and founded the Columbia Society for Comparative Philosophy. He has held teaching posts at Columbia University, The New School, and Brooklyn College.

Christopher Key Chapple is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He served as a professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions (attested 1982) and as Doshi Professor at Loyola Marymount University (attested 2001–2017).
Christopher L. Diamond specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under Heidi Rika Maria Pauwels (~2012–2018) and holds a post at the Australian National University (attested 2026).

Christopher Minkowski is an Indologist educated at Harvard and the University of Delhi. He held positions at Wolfson College, Brown, University of Iowa (~1989–1999), and Cornell (1989–2006) before serving as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford and Balliol College (2005–2023).

Christopher Pinney works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the Australian National University (~1988–1992) and University College London (from ~1993), alongside visiting or faculty roles at Chicago, Cape Town, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Northwestern University.

Christopher S. George works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Columbia University under Royal W. Weiler (1965) and with Geshe Wangyal and Padma Gyaltsan, later founding the American Institute of Buddhist Studies (1972) and teaching at IASWR (1982).

Christopher S. Queen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held academic posts at Harvard University as a lecturer on Buddhism and world religions (~1989) and as Dean of Students for Continuing Education (~1989–2008).

Chu-tsing Li was a scholar of Sinology and art history who studied at the University of Nanking and the University of Iowa. He taught English at Nanking (1943–1947), art history at Iowa (~1956–1965), and joined the University of Kansas faculty in 1966.

Chuan-ying Yen specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at Harvard University, where she studied under Chu-tsing Li, John Hay, and doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield (attested 1986).
Chuichi Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an associate professor (attested 2015) and former professor (attested 2026) at Minobusan University.

Chun-i Tang was a philosopher and Sinologist who studied at Sino-Russian University, Peking University, and National Central University under Thomé H. Fang, Shili Xiong, and others. He taught at Central University, co-founded New Asia College, and chaired philosophy at CUHK (1963–1974).

Chun-min Yen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD at the University of Arizona (attested 2004) under Robert M. Gimello, also studying with Todd Brown and traditional teachers Chanyun and Sheng Yen.

Chögyam Trungpa was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Khenpo Gangshar and at Oxford (1963). He served at the Young Lamas Home School (1959–1963) and founded Kagyu Samye Ling (1967), Naropa University (1973), and Gampo Abbey.

Chökyi Gyatso was a scholar and lineage holder who studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Thubten Chökyi Dorje, Khakyab Dorje, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö; he also taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
